clue.text: Book parts in plays

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book of the New Testament
second meaning: the major divisions of a drama

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about sections of a script; split it after the first word for two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of the Apostles is a biblical book, and plays are divided into acts, each holding several scenes.

clue.text: Mythical creature to agree with sun god

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A fabulous beast is expected to fall into line with the sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek legend was a fire-breathing monster, part lion, part goat, part serpent.

clue.text: Poverty-stricken holy man welcomes in family

indicators.note: a host who welcomes guests in has them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A penniless holy man still opens his door to his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skint means being broke, utterly without cash, which is informal for poverty-stricken.

clue.text: Invalids limit wearing underwear

indicators.note: something worn is enclosed by the garment, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in Britain pants are underpants
to tie someone down is to limit them

explanation.surface: Sick people have restrictions on what they wear beneath their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants means underwear, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Invalids are people who are ill, and those under medical care are patients.

clue.text: Favourite part of Cape Town

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A best-loved district of the South African city.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's pet is the favourite pupil, the one singled out for special treatment.

clue.text: Finish session in a tie, losing heart

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart drops its central letter

parts.note: a school or court session is a term
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A sporting season ends level, and everyone is disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-letter tie loses its middle letter, leaving TE to close TERMINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, a direct verb synonym of finish.

clue.text: Husband succumbing to pressure, urges foreign shipments

indicators.note: one that succumbs to another gives way, so one letter yields its place to a different one

parts.note: to exhort is to urge strongly
H is the abbreviation for husband
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A husband gives in to pressure and presses for goods to be sent abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXHORTS the H makes way for P, giving EXPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods sent out of a country for sale abroad, that is, foreign shipments.

clue.text: Two take time to go on wagon

indicators.note: in a down clue going on top means sitting above, so the first piece precedes the second

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A pair take a while to climb aboard a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: TWAIN is an archaic word for two, as in 'never the twain shall meet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an old poetic word meaning a pair, the number two.

clue.text: One placed in cabinet and one in church

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a government member who heads a department
second meaning: a member of the clergy

explanation.walkthrough: A cabinet looks like furniture to put something away in, but it is the body of senior government members.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a senior politician sitting in government and a cleric serving a congregation.

clue.text: Beg agreement on public relations

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it in an across answer

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for public relations
ay is an old form of yes

explanation.surface: Pleading for consent from the publicity department.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray someone do something is to beseech them, an old-fashioned sense of entreat.

clue.text: Run across flood on the way back

indicators.note: heading back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to teem is to pour or swarm in abundance

explanation.surface: Someone has to dash through high water on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to encounter them by chance, which is to meet them.

clue.text: Stimulating call after fuss

indicators.note: one piece coming after another means it is placed second

parts.note: a stir is a commotion
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: An exciting summons following a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirring speech rouses its audience, so the adjective means exciting or stimulating.

clue.text: Magnificence of recycled old prunes

indicators.note: something recycled is broken down and remade in a new form

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mock praise for the grandeur of reused dried plums.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is grand, impressive beauty, a close noun synonym of magnificence.

clue.text: Lot of Catholics in return of Spring

indicators.note: a thing in another sits inside it
a return goes back the way it came, so the word runs end to start

parts.note: to spring is to jump
RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Many churchgoers come back when the season of Spring returns.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season but is the verb jump.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, a lot is an item or bundle offered for sale, which is also called a parcel.

clue.text: Fashionable before Windy City

parts.note: chic means stylish
ago means in the past, before now

explanation.surface: A stylish place long before it got its gusty nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a positional signal but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City is the long-standing nickname of the big Illinois city on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: A singular sense about withdrawn approval

indicators.note: something withdrawn is taken out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
scent is the sense of smell, or a trace sensed
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A unique feeling about approval being withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal; here it is circa, the C dropped from SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or consent, so giving assent means giving approval.

clue.text: No mail distribution around November, in theory

indicators.note: letters placed around another surround it
a distribution spreads things out into a new arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Supposedly nothing gets delivered at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only, not in practice, so it is so in theory.

clue.text: Huntress mostly in race glowing

definitions.note: a noun, read as the act of glowing

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A huntress shines as she runs in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is the quality of giving off light, a glow, so it matches the noun glowing.

clue.text: Entertain a goddess

parts.note: taken as written
the Muses were Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A host is asked to look after a visiting deity.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse people is to keep them entertained and make them laugh.

clue.text: Bachelor crowd returning a large sum of money

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A single man comes back to the gang with a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English something that costs a bomb costs a great deal of money.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom 'cost a bomb' uses the word for a huge amount of cash.

clue.text: Offspring feel depressed, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a family of young animals
second meaning: to sulk or dwell gloomily

explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' admits that the second meaning is mood-flavoured worry rather than strict depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood is a set of young hatched together; to brood is to mope and dwell on something gloomily.

clue.text: Atmosphere detected in restaurant

indicators.note: something detected inside a word is found lying within its letters

parts.note: lies inside the word

explanation.surface: A diner picks up on the mood of the eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive feeling surrounding a place or person, its atmosphere.

clue.text: Congenial expense

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is mostly plural, outgoings, but a single outgoing is one payment out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person is sociable and friendly; an outgoing is a sum of money paid out.

clue.text: Tip to note

parts.note: taken as written
E is a musical note

explanation.definitionFit: The toe of a shoe or boot is its tip, the front end.

clue.text: Core user adapted source of help

indicators.note: something adapted is altered to a new form

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A central customer modified where they turn for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is something one can turn to for aid when in difficulty, a fallback resource.

clue.text: Ass or donkey only likes thistle first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of every word that follows

parts.note: the initial letters of the last four words

explanation.surface: A donkey is fussy and will eat only thistles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' looks like part of the donkey picture but is the definition, an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, and a dolt is a stupid one.
